# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**Riley Kimura**
Member ID: W548803729
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Avera Health Plans — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on the denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-11**
**Reference number:** POC-F4D8086686-78032
**Member:** Riley Kimura | **Member ID:** W548803729
**Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Governing policy:** Cohere Medical Policy - Shoulder Arthroscopy (Version 5), Avera Health Plans — https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines#shoulder-arthroscopy-v5

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-11 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria under the Shoulder Arthroscopy policy cited above describe the findings that are already documented in my records.

I am writing about the imaging finding first, since that is the reason the plan gave.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The imaging requirement**

The policy states:

> "Advanced imaging with radiologist report that demonstrates ANY of the following:"

and among the findings it lists:

> "Full-thickness rotator cuff tear; OR"

My MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-07-11 shows a **full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy**. A full-thickness rotator cuff tear is the first finding named in the plan's own list. If the complete radiologist report did not reach the reviewer, I am asking that it be requested and reviewed before a final decision is made, and I am enclosing a copy: [copy of the 2026-07-11 MRI radiologist report, if not already on file].

**2. Pain and functional impairment**

The policy states:

> "Significant pain or functional impairment that impacts activities of daily living (ADLs); AND"

My records document 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

**3. Chronic tear and conservative management**

The policy allows for either an acute or a chronic tear:

> "Documentation of an acute rotator cuff tear (RCT) after an inciting event or injury; OR"

> "Documentation of a chronic RCT and ALL of the following22:"

My symptoms have been present and worsening for 24 months, so my records are addressed to the chronic pathway, which requires:

> "Failure of conservative managementA, including ALL of the following:"

- **Medication.** The policy requires: *"Anti-inflammatory medications, non-opioid analgesics, neuropathic medications, or other pain medications, if not contraindicated; AND"* — My records document **NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief**.
- **Therapy.** The policy requires: *"Physical therapy (PT) and/or documentation of patient compliance with a home exercise prescription/plan (HEP) provided by a physician or physical therapist targeting the requested region; AND"* — I completed **supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 16 visits over 12 weeks, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03**, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This was shoulder-directed therapy, targeting the region being requested.
- **Duration.** The policy states: *"PT/HEP trialed for a duration of 3 months or more; OR"* and, in the alternative, *"Progression or worsening of symptoms due to PT/HEP; AND"* — My therapy course ran from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, and my symptoms are documented as progressive over 24 months and unrelieved by rest.
- **Injection.** The policy requires: *"Corticosteroid injection if medically appropriate10; OR"* (or, alternatively, *"Documentation that corticosteroid injection is contraindicated; OR"*) — I received a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-22, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief** before my symptoms returned.

The policy also provides:

> "The patient has completed a full course of conservative management without meaningful improvement.
> Patient noncompliance, closure of therapy offices, and patient inconvenience do not constitute a failure of
> conservative treatment."

I want to be clear that none of those exclusions apply to me. I attended 16 physical therapy visits, took anti-inflammatory medication for four months, and had an injection. I completed the treatment that was asked of me, and I still cannot raise my arm over my head or sleep on that shoulder.

**4. Documentation in the file**

The policy states:

> "Documentation must include a recent and detailed history, physical examination related to the onset or change in symptoms, relevant lab results, prior imaging, and details of previous treatments."

My prior authorization packet contains a symptom history covering 24 months, examination findings, the 2026-07-11 MRI, and a detailed record of medication, injection, and physical therapy with dates and visit counts. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoking status. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

I should note that several of the excerpts above end in a colon and introduce further conditions in the policy that I was not able to obtain in full. If the plan applied any criterion from those lists, I am asking that it be identified specifically so I can respond to it.

## Request for the criteria used

Please provide me, in writing, with the exact clinical criteria that were applied to this denial, including the name and edition of any clinical review guideline used, and the specific criterion the reviewer found unmet. The plan holds these criteria, and I am entitled to receive them. If the denial rests on a finding, threshold, or measurement that is not quoted above, please state it plainly so that my surgeon and I can address it directly.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Avera Health Plans overturn the denial dated 2026-08-11 and authorize the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by Dr. Reyes. If the determination is not overturned, please send me a written explanation identifying each criterion found unmet and the records reviewed, along with information about my right to further review, including external review.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-07**, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; any member who is unsure where to send an appeal can call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for taking another look at my file. I am glad to provide any additional records you need.

Sincerely,

**Riley Kimura**
Member ID: W548803729
Reference number: POC-F4D8086686-78032
[Phone] | [Email]

**Enclosures:** [MRI report dated 2026-07-11]; [physical therapy discharge note]; [office notes from Dr. Reyes]; [medication and injection records]; [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-11]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
